title: Compliance Event Bridge: guaranteed delivery, schema, and retention control APIs
creator: Ariana Cole
description: Build an internal "event bridge" and public-facing Compliance Events API to centralize, persist, and deliver residency, retention, and audit evidence events to downstream consumers (customers' webhooks, SIEMs, and internal analytics). Goals: durable delivery with retries and backoff, clear versioned schema for event types, per-customer residency/retention metadata attachment, admin controls for event export/TTL, and signed payloads for authenticity. This work includes API contract, internal queueing guarantees, operational metrics, and a rollout plan that preserves privacy/residency constraints for Private deployments.
acceptance_criteria: Event API exposes stable, versioned schemas for residency, retention-change, and audit-evidence events (JSON Schema v1 documented on Confluence).
Webhooks delivered with at-least-once semantics and documented idempotency keys (event_id + sequence).
Delivery guarantees configurable per-customer: retries/backoff policy and dead-letter visibility in Console.
Payloads are signed using HMAC with rotating keys; verification doc and SDK helpers provided for Node/Python/Go.
Internal retention settings applied to stored evidence with per-tenant TTLs and automated purging; retention toggles respect customer residency (region) constraints.
E2E tests and a small canary rollout demonstrate successful delivery to 3 sample customers and a simulated VPC endpoint.
implementation_plan: Phase 1: API & schema design (Confluence: /display/Compliance/EventBridgeSpec) + design review (2 days).
Phase 2: Internal queue + delivery worker: durable work queue (db-backed + redis lease) and delivery engine with concurrency limits (Marcus).
Phase 3: Signing & key rotation service: implement HMAC signer, key rotation endpoint, and SDK helper functions.
Phase 4: Console controls: admin UI for per-tenant retry policy, TTL, and DLQ inspection (Design: DES-2042 follow-up).
Phase 5: Private deployment checklist: document VPC egress patterns, proxying options, and local delivery adapters.
Phase 6: Testing & rollout: integration tests, chaos injection for delivery failures, canary to 5% of customers, full rollout after 2 weeks of stability.
decisions: Use at-least-once delivery + idempotency rather than full exactly-once to avoid cross-service distributed transactions.
Signed payloads will use HMAC-SHA256 with per-tenant rotating keys (simpler to verify in customer infrastructure than JWT).
Event store will persist a small canonical representation (event header + minimal payload) for evidence queries; large attachments remain in object storage with short-lived signed URLs.
Schema will be versioned (v1/v2) and validated at write-time; old versions will be retained for 90 days and deprecated via console notices.
tradeoffs: Durability vs Latency: buffering/acks increase end-to-end latency; we provide opt-in synchronous delivery for critical audit flows at higher cost.
Signing strategy: HMAC chosen over asymmetric signatures to avoid key distribution complexity for customers behind strict firewalls, at the cost of weaker non-repudiation.
Storage: keeping minimal canonical event improves query speed and privacy but requires a separate blob store for large evidence items which complicates purging semantics.
